fields.name: matter_number
fields.hint: the matter number, verbatim from the Matter Number section

fields.name: order_date
fields.hint: the date this Order was entered, from the Order Date section, converted to YYYY-MM-DD. The Order writes dates in words ('11 February 2027'); every date you return is ISO

fields.name: deadlines
fields.hint: one object per numbered paragraph that SETS A DEADLINE. Do NOT return an object for a paragraph that merely mentions a date, sets a page limit, or states a deadline and then strikes, withdraws, vacates or supersedes it — those set no date and produce no row. Return the objects in paragraph order

subfields.name: paragraph
subfields.hint: the paragraph's own number in the Deadlines Ordered section. This is the join key — copy it exactly

subfields.name: item
subfields.hint: what must be done, verbatim and in the lower case the paragraph states it — for example 'initial disclosures', 'the joint status report'. Do not add words the paragraph does not use

subfields.name: basis
subfields.hint: how this paragraph fixes its date. 'on or before <date>' or 'no later than <date>' is explicit_date. 'within N days of/after the date of this Order' is calendar_days_from_order. 'within N days after <a recorded event>' is calendar_days_from_event. The same two with 'business days' are the business_ variants

subfields.name: period_days
subfields.hint: N, the number of days the paragraph counts — null for explicit_date. Return the number only, not the unit; the unit is already in `basis`

subfields.name: trigger_event
subfields.hint: the triggering event the period runs from, copied verbatim from the Recorded Events table — null for explicit_date and for anything counted from the date of this Order. 'the date of this Order' is NOT an event and is never this value

subfields.name: trigger_event_date
subfields.hint: the date the Recorded Events table gives for that event, as YYYY-MM-DD. Null when the table says 'not recorded', and null when there is no trigger event. NEVER substitute the Order date for a missing event date

subfields.name: stated_date
subfields.hint: the date the paragraph names in words, as YYYY-MM-DD — only for explicit_date, null otherwise

subfields.name: party_calculated_date
subfields.hint: the date in the parenthetical a party wrote next to the obligation ('counsel's calendar: 19 March 2027'), as YYYY-MM-DD, or null when the paragraph carries none. Copy it as a field. IT IS NOT THE ANSWER and it is wrong on some of these orders

subfields.name: due_date
subfields.hint: the calendar date this obligation actually falls due, as YYYY-MM-DD, computed by the COUNTING RULES given above and by nothing else. Null — and only null — when the period runs from a triggering event the Order does not date. Never copy party_calculated_date into this field, and never fall back to the Order date for an undated event
